$meta.about: The one token source for the estate. Every generated file (generated/tokens.css, generated/tokens.ts, python/estate_kit/tokens.py, generated/pptx-theme.json) is built from this file by scripts/build-tokens.mjs and checked against it by tests/tokens-parity.test.ts. Edit this file, then run npm run tokens.

skins.proposed: None of the three editorial sites has a dark theme, and two have no light accent beyond the deep one, so these were derived by scripts/derive-skin-dark.mjs on 11 November 2026 and wait on the owner: each dark paper, warm paper and line is the kit's dark bg, bg-subtle and border mixed 6, 8 and 12 per cent towards the deep accent; the bright accent is the deep one mixed towards white until it clears 4.5:1 on all three dark grounds (UK AI keeps its own --accent-bright, which already does); the dark wash is the dark paper mixed 12 per cent towards the bright accent; a missing light wash is the deep accent at 8 per cent over the paper; the soft neutral (series-neutral-soft, #8b939c) clears 3:1 on white but only 2.88 on UK AI's paper, which the skin gate found in BillAnatomy, so each editorial skin overrides it with the kit's value moved towards the text colour until it clears 3:1 on paper, warm paper and card. tests/skins.test.ts gates every value in both themes.

skins.about: A skin per site, beside its accent triple: a paper triple (paper, warm paper, line) for each theme, a display scale that reaches hero size, a display face with an italic slot and the body face, a section rhythm, a radius pair and a motion set (one easing, two durations under 300 ms, both set to 0ms by a reduced motion guard), and, where a kit colour fails on the skin's paper, an override of that colour. A site entry names its register and inherits that register's skin; an editorial entry gives its own values, each quoted in $meta.sources.skins. A record entry may carry its own paper, radius and overrides where the site's own stylesheet holds them (Council Intel), each quoted in $meta.sources.skins; a record entry without them reproduces the kit exactly. Keys listed in proposed were derived by scripts/derive-skin-dark.mjs, not read from the site, and wait on the owner.

record.about: For the data sites: restrained, dense, colour kept for data. Every value is one the kit already ships, so a record site's output does not change.

face.sans: "Source Sans 3", -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

editorial.about: For UK AI, Lancashire AI and Tour de France Lancashire: tinted paper, display type at hero scale with an italic, a wide section rhythm, more motion. The three already share this skeleton (RETHINK_2026-11.md section 3.1), so each entry gives its own values and the register adds none.

desk.about: A desk is a dark ground band inside a light page, in both themes: its ground, ink, muted text, rule, the three state colours drawn on it and each state's ink on its badge ground. A skin that has one lists its values under desk; generated CSS sets them as --ground, --ground-ink, --ground-muted, --ground-rule, --ground-positive and so on, and a [data-ground="desk"] rule points the kit's names at them, so text, rules and a chart in css mode inside the band take the desk's values. names maps each kit name to a desk key, to another kit name (kit:accent-bright), or to the kit's dark value of a name (dark:series-1): the series and neutrals on the desk are the kit's dark set, which is validated for a dark ground. There is no wash on the desk, so accent-wash is the ground.

aliases.about: Each site's legacy custom property names, mapped to kit names, written by the token build as generated/aliases/<site>.css: a block a site splices below the kit's estate-tokens block (and below its skin block), so the next splice of the kit leaves it alone. One list per name set; a site names the set it uses. Nothing new may use these names; they go as each template is rewritten. Decision D in RETHINK_2026-11.md.

pre-system-2026-08.about: The 28 names the pre system stylesheet used, mapped when UK Demographics moved to the estate block on 29 August 2026 and copied by UK Council Tax. --tooltip-bg and --tooltip-fg are not here: the kit block sets both themes of each, and a copy below it would undo the dark values.

print.about: Print sheets: the page box, faces, type sizes in points, leading and colours of a printed surface. A sheet is not a site and has no dark theme. It is generated as generated/print/<sheet>.css (an @page rule and a block of --print-* custom properties between estate-print markers) and read in Python with print_tokens(). The values are the surface's own, quoted in $meta.sources.print, so taking the sheet changes nothing on the page.

brief.about: The house brief that Reports tools/md2pdf.py prints: A4, a serif body under sans headings, navy headings and table heads, one red accent.
